notes: L3 is not a real problem. The booklet builds four separate models: the mini-doll Emma (p.2), the plant pot (p.3), the sun lounger with umbrella and goblet (pp.4-8) and the splash pool with steps (pp.9-12). Each is introduced by its own inset picture, and page 13 only shows them standing side by side. Nothing fastens them together, so the groups stay disconnected.

L1 is not a real problem. The parts page prints each of these once as 3x 4618924 and 1x 4527943. The extracted text repeats those two entries at the bottom of the page, which is a text-extraction duplicate, not extra pieces. The pictures show one 1x lime round brick (plant pot) and three trans-green windscreen panels in the pool. I kept 3 and 1 to match the page images.
The minifig ports use ball/socket kinds (head top = ball, neck = socket, torso neck = ball, torso waist = socket, legs waist = ball). Hair socket fits the head-top ball.
The umbrella rod 4538720 has a hollow lower end that pushes over the round brick's stud, so its end.1 is kind anti-stud. Its upper end (end.2) goes into the umbrella dish's axle hole.

The sun lounger layering is ambiguous in the pictures. I assumed the 2x4 plate carries the pink 2x2 brick and the 2x6 plate overlaps it. The 2x6 plate carries the slope, the four tiles and the two lime feet.

The pool step stacking is also ambiguous. I assumed two 2x2 white plates are stacked on the pink floor, with a 1x2 white plate beside them. Each carries one lime tile. The exact pairings of the four pink curved plates, four aqua curved bricks and three windscreens are approximate.
To avoid reusing a single-use port, I numbered studs and anti-studs. Where a catalogue port was not available (soil underside, goblet cup, leaf centre stud), the port is left null.
The set has 5 lime 1x2 tiles: 2 on the lounger and 3 on the pool steps. The set has 3 orange flowers: plant, goblet and umbrella. Lime round plate 4183133 (x2, the lounger feet) is in the catalogue.
